name: drg-0001-goal1
goal: Outline every neuron cell body and count them, leaving out the satellite glia and Schwann cells around them.

look.notes: The image is a fluorescence microscopy image of a rat dorsal root ganglion section stained with an anti-neurofilament antibody. The structures visible are neurons, with their nuclei and neurofilament-positive processes. The approximate number of neurons in the whole section is 10,000. The images are at different magnifications: image 1 (overview, 1.52 µm/pixel), image 2 and 3 (high magnification, 0.48 µm/pixel).

not_possible: Counting neurons in the whole section is not possible because the image resolution (1.52 µm/pixel) is too coarse to reliably distinguish individual cell bodies from the dense background and overlapping structures. The pixel size (0.95 µm) is also insufficient for precise cell body segmentation at this scale.

steps.why: To locate potential neuron cell bodies by identifying nuclei, which are the most reliable morphological markers for neurons in this stain. The nuclei are typically round to oval and darker than the surrounding cytoplasm.
steps.marker: Neurofilament (NF) stain intensity (if split_by_marker is used for segmentation, but not necessary for initial detection).

steps.why: To segment and outline every nucleus that matches the cell model (neuron nucleus) based on shape, size, and intensity. This will provide a more accurate outline than find_by_text, especially for overlapping or irregular nuclei.
steps.marker: Neurofilament (NF) stain intensity (optional for split_by_marker if needed for segmentation).

steps.why: To count the number of neuron cell bodies (nuclei) in the whole section. This will give an estimate of the total number of neurons.
steps.marker: Neurofilament (NF) stain intensity (optional for split_by_marker if needed for segmentation).

plan.result: The analysis will outline and count neuron cell bodies (nuclei) based on their size and shape, using the Neurofilament stain as a marker. The count will be an estimate of the total number of neurons in the section.
risks: The resolution may not be sufficient to distinguish neuron cell bodies from satellite glia or Schwann cells, especially in the dense regions. This could lead to overcounting or undercounting.
The nuclei may overlap or be obscured by the dense background, making segmentation and counting difficult.
The Neurofilament stain may not be specific enough to distinguish neurons from other cell types, especially if the stain is weak or unevenly distributed.
